paragraphs: Friend, listen to how this starts. David says to himself, "One of these days now I will be swept away by the hand of Saul." (1 Samuel 27:1) But earlier, Saul had blessed him and gone home (1 Samuel 26:25). I think David let his fear do the math instead of letting what he'd just seen do it.

Now look at where that fear walks him. He ends up in Philistine territory, living under King Achish, and Achish trusts him because of what he tells him. He keeps his raids hidden with a story, and the text even says Achish thinks, "he will be my servant forever." (1 Samuel 27:12) The passage doesn't tell us what David should have done, and I won't guess. But it shows what happens when we start managing our own escape: we end up in a spot we never planned to stand in.

This part is heavy, and I think it should be. Here's what I take from it, friend. The Bible shows us real people at their most worried, and it doesn't hide the mess. So when you catch yourself saying, "One of these days now..." and building a whole plan around it, stop and look at what's actually in front of you. This story is NOT done, and I'm not going to tell you how it ends.
